prior_s_pneumoniae.byte_quote: The most common pathogens were Streptococcus pneumoniae (51 percent of episodes) and Neisseria meningitidis (37 percent).

prior_n_meningitidis.byte_quote: As per Thigpen etal. out of the 1670 cases reported in the U.S. during 2003–2007, S. pneumoniae was the predominant infective species (58.0%), followed by GBS (18.1%), N. meningitidis (13.9%), H. influenzae (6.7%), and L. monocytogenes (3.4%).

prior_h_influenzae.byte_quote: As per Thigpen etal. out of the 1670 cases reported in the U.S. during 2003–2007, S. pneumoniae was the predominant infective species (58.0%), followed by GBS (18.1%), N. meningitidis (13.9%), H. influenzae (6.7%), and L. monocytogenes (3.4%).

prior_listeria.byte_quote: Listeria monocytogenes (182/2974; 6%) ... Patients with listeria meningitis were more likely to be immunocompromised (121/182 [66%] vs. 791/2791 [28%]) ... Mortality was highest for L. monocytogenes (58/182; 32%)

prior_gram_negative_bacilli.byte_quote: Gram-negative bacilli (other than Haemophilus influenzae) caused 33 percent of the nosocomial episodes but only 3 percent of the community-acquired episodes.

prior_group_b_strep.byte_quote: The frequency of group B S. agalactiae in neonates was highest in Europe and lowest in the Eastern Mediterranean region, with weighted means of 58.2% and 4.9%, respectively.

morph_gpd_pneumococcus.byte_quote: Cells of S pneumoniae are elongated ("lancet-shaped") cocci that are surrounded by a polysaccharide capsule and predominantly organized in pairs (diplococci).

morph_gnd_meningococcus.byte_quote: Intracellular gram-negative diplococci and leukocytes in the CSF from a patient with meningococcal meningitis. The arrow denotes diplococci in proximity and within leukocytes.

morph_gpb_listeria.byte_quote: gram-positive bacilli with tumbling motility ... This characteristic of L. monocytogenes is evident through peritrichous flagella movement and is clinically useful to corroborate high suspicion of Listeria infection before the confirmatory microbiological examination.

morph_gncocco_hflu.byte_quote: The initial test is Gram staining, which reveals pleomorphic gram-negative coccobacilli.

morph_gnb_enteric.byte_quote: H. influenzae, a fastidious, pleomorphic, gram-negative coccobacillus, requires hemin (X factor) ... A Gram stain of an infected body fluid may demonstrate small, gram-negative coccobacilli suggestive of H. influenzae disease.

morph_gpcc_saureus.byte_quote: Gram-positive cocci include Staphylococcus (catalase-positive), which grows clusters, and Streptococcus (catalase-negative), which grows in chains.
